 Kim Arim Fires a 7-Under... 'Going for the Season Finale Win~'
 by Roh Woolae 
 Published 20 Nov.2026 08:08(KST) 
 Share 
 Language 
 Text Size 
 Print 
 Tied for the lead with Thitikul in the first round of the CME Group Tour Championship
Haeran Ryu, Hyejin Choi and Somi Lee tied for fourth, one shot back
Korda, Ina Yoon and Yamashita tied for 20th, chasing the leaders
 Kim Arim got off to a flying start in the season finale.
 Kim Arim made nine birdies and two bogeys in the first round of the CME Group Tour Championship, an LPGA Tour event with an $11 million purse, at Tiburon Golf Club (par 72) in Naples, Florida, on Nov. 20 (Korea time). Her seven-under-par 65 put her in a tie for the lead with world No. 1 Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand and Caris Davidson of Australia.
 Kim A-rim (left) and Arpichaya Yubol embrace after finishing the first round of the CME Group Tour Championship. Naples=AFP Yonhap News
 View original image 
 Kim made three birdies over the first nine holes but also had two bogeys, resulting in an up-and-down front nine. She showed her resilience on the back nine, making six birdies without a bogey. Kim won the 2020 U.S. Women's Open, a major championship, and made her LPGA Tour debut the following year. She earned her third career victory at the 2024 LOTTE Championship and the Hilton Grand Vacations Tournament of Champions in January 2025.
 In an official interview after the first round, Kim said, "I feel comfortable here because I've played here six times," adding, "My putts were going in, and my shots were good. I was able to get into a good rhythm."
 Haeran Ryu, Hyejin Choi and Somi Lee are chasing the leaders, tied for fourth at six-under-par 66, one shot back. "I didn't play well on Florida courses when I was a rookie," Ryu said with a smile. "But I've been doing better than before lately, and I think today's round is making me a fan of Florida courses."

 World No. 1 Nelly Korda of the United States carded a four-under-par 68 to sit in a tie for 20th. A win at this tournament would earn Korda the points she needs to qualify for the LPGA Hall of Fame. Ina Yoon and Miyu Yamashita of Japan are also tied for 20th. Hyo Joo Kim is tied for 50th at even-par 72.
